screening_decisions.reason: This is a before-after observational study comparing PHC villages with non-PHC villages. No randomization was used; villages were assigned based on size (too small to join PHC programme). Does not meet RCT criterion.

While this is an RCT, the intervention being tested is malaria chemoprophylaxis (Maloprim vs placebo), not TBA training. TBAs were merely the delivery mechanism for the drug. Does not compare trained vs untrained TBAs.
This is an observational comparative study with three groups (TBA, tetanus toxoid, control). No randomization mentioned. Does not meet RCT criterion.

This study focuses on TBAs managing childhood pneumonia, not pregnancy outcomes or TBA training for childbirth. The intervention is pneumonia treatment training, not standard TBA training for maternal/newborn care.
This is a Cochrane review protocol, not a primary study. Reviews do not meet the inclusion criteria for primary RCTs.
Methodological paper about detecting bias in meta-analyses using funnel plots. Not related to TBA training or pregnancy outcomes.
Survey validation study examining recall accuracy of obstetric complications. Not an RCT and not about TBA training.

This is an RCT comparing two educational approaches (lecture-style vs interactive problem-based) for training TBAs. Fits the 'additionally trained versus trained' criterion as both groups received training but with different methods.

Primary intervention is home-based neonatal care by village health workers. TBAs were part of a broader package but not the focus. The comparison is intervention vs control villages receiving comprehensive neonatal care, not specifically TBA training.

Controlled study comparing communities with access to trained TBAs vs communities without access. Uses randomly selected comparable communities. Compares women living in areas served by trained TBAs vs those without such access. Meets the criterion for 'women cared for/living in areas served by TBAs'.
This is a critical review/commentary on a meta-analysis, not a primary study. Does not meet RCT criterion.

Explicitly a cluster randomised controlled trial. Birth attendants were cluster randomised to intervention (training in neonatal resuscitation + amoxicillin) vs control (standard care). Directly compares trained vs untrained TBAs on neonatal mortality outcomes.
Narrative review/opinion article summarizing evidence from systematic reviews. Not a primary RCT.
Retrospective case series from a tertiary hospital. Not about TBA training and not an RCT.
Time-series experimental study (pre-post design) assessing knowledge and referral practices. No control group and no randomization. Does not meet RCT criterion.

Cluster-randomized controlled trial. Seven subdistricts randomly assigned to intervention (TBAs trained + delivery kits + integration with health system) vs control (usual care). Directly compares areas with trained TBAs integrated into health system vs usual care.

While this is a cluster RCT, the primary intervention is women's groups for participatory action learning. Both intervention and control clusters received basic TBA training, so it does not compare trained vs untrained TBAs. The focus is on women's groups, not TBA training.
Systematic review analyzing causes of maternal death across multiple datasets. Not a primary RCT and not about TBA training.
Quasi-experimental design (not randomized). Uses before-after comparison with geographical controls. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
Cluster RCT but the intervention is exclusive breastfeeding promotion by health/nutrition workers, not TBA training. Outcomes are infant feeding and diarrhoea, not pregnancy/maternal outcomes.
Longitudinal quasi-experimental study comparing intervention and comparison areas, not a randomised controlled trial (RCT).
Observational community-based study comparing delivery locations, not an RCT.
Commentary/review article on the Safe Motherhood Initiative, not an RCT.
Abstract describes a qualitative study on Episcopal priests' identity work, completely unrelated to the review topic.
Cluster RCT evaluating nutrition counselling by health and nutrition workers; TBAs are only mentioned as one of many counselling channels, not the focus of training or comparison.
Methodological paper on statistical tests for meta-analysis, not an RCT on TBA training.

Cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluating training of community-based birth attendants (TBAs) in Essential Newborn Care and Neonatal Resuscitation Program versus control; meets all selection criteria.
Prospective observational study assessing accuracy of women's recall of obstetric complications, not an RCT.
Cross-sectional survey of TBA knowledge and practices, not an RCT.
Quasi-experimental study comparing intervention and non-intervention areas for TBA-administered misoprostol; not explicitly randomised.
Review article on global neonatal mortality epidemiology, not an RCT.
Cluster RCT evaluating an intervention delivered by Lady Health Workers (LHWs); TBAs are mentioned as collaborators but the training/intervention targets LHWs, not TBAs.
Methodological validation study of verbal autopsy for neonatal deaths, not an RCT.
